# Sprint bk-5 — hook and cron CLI, doctor hooks section, composition, user docs closure_type `integration`; target_boundary the `atm` CLI (`atm hook`, `atm cron`, the `atm doctor` hooks section) and the daemon composition of `atm-cron`, over `req:REQ-P-HOOK-001`, `req:REQ-P-HOOK-003`, `req:REQ-P-HOOK-004`, `req:REQ-P-CRON-001`, `req:REQ-P-CRON-002`; branch `sprint/bk-5-hook-cli-doctor`, PR → the stack top above bk-4 (`sprint/bk-4-atm-cron`); difficulty normal; recommended_agent `arch-ctm`, recommended_model `gpt-5-codex`. Consumes bk-1 (the seven codes), bk-2 (the six request envelopes and their responses, `HookActionsResponse`, `HookDoctorEntry`, `DoctorReport.hooks`, `HookName`, `PhaseId`, `StopCondition`, `HTTP_API_VERSION 1.13.0`), bk-3 (the six routes, `X-ATM-Hook-Actions`, the router's `hook_runner` field, `install_cron_scheduler`, the four-tuple of `build_replacement_handler`, `fixture_hook.py`) and bk-4 (`AtmCron`, `AtmCronDeps`, `CronWorkerHandle`, `SystemClock`, `SystemJitter`). Governing text: `design.md` §2.3, §5, §6, §9.1, §9.7, §9.8, §9.9, §9.10, D-2, D-5, D-9; `REQ-P-HOOK-003` §23.1, `REQ-P-HOOK-004` §11.5, `REQ-P-CRON-001` §24.1, `REQ-P-CRON-002` §24.2, `REQ-P-USER-DOCS-001`; ADR-068 D3, D5, D6, ADR-069 D1, D2, ADR-066. ## Scope boundary This sprint owns the user-facing surface. That is the two CLI commands, the `TIMEOUT_MS` read, the exit-code arms, the doctor collection and rendering, the CLI surface baseline, the user documentation, and the composition of `atm-cron` into the daemon. It creates no storage, protocol, runner, filter, route or scheduler code. It edits no file under `crates/atm-cron` or `crates/atm-core`. `crates/atm/Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]` is unchanged. Owned paths (new unless marked edited): - `crates/atm/src/commands/hook.rs`, `crates/atm/src/commands/cron.rs`, `crates/atm/src/commands/hook_module.rs`, `crates/atm/src/commands/mod.rs` (edited: `Hook(HookCommand)`, `Cron(CronCommand)` in `enum Command` at `:118` and their arms), `crates/atm/src/output.rs` (edited: `print_hook_list`, `print_cron_list`, the hooks block in `print_doctor_result` at `:288`, the `HookActions` line), `crates/atm/src/main.rs` (edited: `HookModuleInvalid`, `HookRefused`, `CronExprInvalid` in the `=> 3` arm of `exit_code_for_atm_error`, `:138-151`) - `crates/atm/tests/cli_surface_baseline.json` (edited), `crates/atm/tests/hook_cli.rs`, `crates/atm/tests/cron_cli.rs`, `crates/atm/tests/fixtures/hook_module/` (`valid_hook.py`, `no_timeout.py`, `zero_timeout.py`, `over_cap.py`, `indented.py`, `two_lines.py`, `cron_timeout.py` with `CRON_TIMEOUT_MS = 20000`, `cron_over_cap.py` with `CRON_TIMEOUT_MS = 30001`) - `crates/atm-http-runtime/src/doctor_hooks.rs` (new), `crates/atm-http-runtime/src/storage_and_nudge_router.rs` (edited: the `doctor()` body at `:651`, one call), `crates/atm-http-runtime/src/lib.rs` (edited: mod) - `crates/atm-daemon-bootstrap/src/lib.rs` (edited: `DaemonWorkers.cron: Option` at `:532`, the composition in `run_replacement_daemon_with_selector` (`:445`), the shutdown step in `shutdown_replacement_daemon` (`:805`)), `crates/atm-daemon-bootstrap/Cargo.toml` (edited: `atm-cron.workspace = true`), `crates/atm-daemon-bootstrap/tests/cron_composition.rs`, `crates/atm-daemon-bootstrap/tests/cron_fixture/fixture_cron.py` - `boundaries/atm-daemon-bootstrap/replacement-bootstrap.toml` and `boundaries/atm-daemon-bootstrap/daemon-observability.toml` (edited: `atm-cron` in `allowed_dependencies`, the latter at `:25`; `cron_worker_lifecycle` in `io_owns` of the former), `boundaries/atm-cron/cron-scheduler.toml` (edited: `[status]` notes the composition), `.just/lint-config.toml` (edited: `atm-cron` in the `crates/atm-daemon-bootstrap/Cargo.toml` allowlist) - `docs/user-documents/cli-reference.md` (edited: `` ### `atm cron` `` and `` ### `atm hook` `` in alphabetical position, a hooks paragraph under `` ### `atm doctor` `` at `:109`), `docs/user-documents/tasks.md` (edited: "Task hooks"), `docs/user-documents/hooks.md` (new) ## Public contract ```rust // crates/atm/src/commands/hook.rs (clap, pattern of task.rs:41) #[derive(Debug, Parser)] pub struct HookCommand { #[command(subcommand)] pub command: HookSubcommand } #[derive(Debug, Subcommand)] pub enum HookSubcommand { Register(HookRegisterArgs), Disable(HookDisableArgs), List(HookListArgs) } #[derive(Debug, Args)] pub struct HookRegisterArgs { pub hook: String, #[arg(long)] pub module: PathBuf, #[arg(long)] pub phase: String, #[arg(long)] pub cwd: Option, #[arg(long, value_parser = parse_custom_object)] pub custom: Option> } // absent sends {} #[derive(Debug, Args)] pub struct HookDisableArgs { #[arg(long)] pub phase: String, pub hook: Option } #[derive(Debug, Args)] pub struct HookListArgs { #[arg(long)] pub phase: Option, #[arg(long)] pub json: bool } // crates/atm/src/commands/cron.rs #[derive(Debug, Subcommand)] pub enum CronSubcommand { Start(CronStartArgs), End(CronEndArgs), List(CronListArgs) } #[derive(Debug, Args)] #[command(group = clap::ArgGroup::new("stop").required(true).multiple(false).args(["until", "until_hook"]))] pub struct CronStartArgs { pub name: String, #[arg(long = "cron")] pub cron_expr: String, #[arg(long)] pub module: PathBuf, #[arg(long)] pub phase: String, #[arg(long, value_parser = parse_rfc3339_utc)] pub until: Option>, #[arg(long = "until-hook")] pub until_hook: bool, #[arg(long = "arg", action = clap::ArgAction::Append, allow_hyphen_values = true)] pub args: Vec, // design D-j: --arg status --arg --json #[arg(long)] pub cwd: Option, #[arg(long, value_parser = parse_custom_object)] pub custom: Option> } #[derive(Debug, Args)] pub struct CronEndArgs { #[arg(long)] pub phase: String, pub name: Option } #[derive(Debug, Args)] pub struct CronListArgs { #[arg(long)] pub phase: Option, #[arg(long)] pub json: bool } // crates/atm/src/commands/hook_module.rs (design.md §9.8 grammar, std only) pub fn read_timeout_ms(module: &Path) -> Result; // Err is AtmError::hook_module_invalid naming the module and the rule broken /// CRON_TIMEOUT_MS by the same grammar, capped at CRON_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS (30 000); absent: read_timeout_ms (Rand 2026-10-18). pub fn read_cron_timeout_ms(module: &Path) -> Result; pub fn parse_custom_object(raw: &str) -> Result, String>; // "--custom must be a JSON object: " // crates/atm/src/output.rs pub fn print_hook_list(rows: &[HookRegistration], json: bool) -> Result<()>; // PHASE HOOK ACTIVE MODULE CWD TIMEOUT_MS CUSTOM REGISTERED_BY REGISTERED_AT DISABLED_AT pub fn print_cron_list(rows: &[CronSchedule], json: bool) -> Result<()>; // PHASE NAME ACTIVE CRON JITTER_S MODULE ARGS TIMEOUT_MS CUSTOM STOP LAST_RUN_AT LAST_OUTCOME // CUSTOM prints ` keys`; --json carries the full custom object and jitter_s // crates/atm-http-runtime/src/doctor_hooks.rs (design.md §9.10) pub(crate) async fn collect(router: &StorageAndNudgeRouter, team: Option<&TeamName>, deadline: RequestDeadline) -> Vec; // rows: the team's active hook_registration rows and the active rows of the installed CronScheduler::list(team, None) (none when not installed); // a schedule becomes a HookRegistration for HookRunner::doctor as bk-4 builds one for a tick; groups by (module_path, cwd, team, phase). ``` Each command does these steps: - **Preflight.** Every command calls `preflight_daemon_api(.., "1.13.0", ..)` (`send.rs:717`) and takes its team from caller context (ADR-066). - **`hook register`.** - It reads `read_timeout_ms` and refuses a value above `HOOK_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS`. - `--cwd` defaults to the module's parent directory. Module and cwd are canonicalized. - It sends `HookRegister` with `custom` from `--custom` and prints `registered for / (timeout ms)`. - It does not check the hook name. The daemon's `ATM_HOOK_MODULE_INVALID` message is printed unchanged. - **`hook disable`.** It prints one line per row changed. With none it prints `no active hooks for phase

` and exits 0. - **`cron start`.** - It reads `read_cron_timeout_ms` (`CRON_TIMEOUT_MS`, else `TIMEOUT_MS`, at most 30 000) and sends `CronStart` with `stop` taken from the clap group and `custom` from `--custom`. - It does not check the expression. `ATM_CRON_EXPR_INVALID` is printed unchanged. - **`list --json`.** It prints a bare JSON array, and `[]` when there are no rows. Human mode prints `none`. `STOP` is `until ` or `hook`. - **Task commands.** A `HookActions` response prints `hook ran actions` (design D-b). A refused task command prints the hook's message and exits 3. Composition (design §9.9). In `run_replacement_daemon_with_selector`, after `build_replacement_handler` (`:471`) returns `(handler, recovery, hook_runner, base_dispatcher)`: ```rust let cron = Arc::new(atm_cron::AtmCron::new(atm_cron::AtmCronDeps { store: runtime.cron_schedule_store()?, runner: hook_runner.clone(), dispatcher: base_dispatcher.clone(), clock: Arc::new(atm_cron::SystemClock), jitter: Arc::new(atm_cron::SystemJitter), host: daemon_atm_config(&env).and_then(|c| c.local_host) })); handler.install_cron_scheduler(cron.clone())?; // after start_replacement_runtime_or_abort (:503) returns Ok and before emit_ready_signal_if_requested (:624): workers.cron = Some(cron.start_worker().await?); // an initial active_all error aborts startup // shutdown_replacement_daemon (:805): shutdown_probe::step("cron_worker", ..) is the first step, before "listener" ``` `docs/user-documents/hooks.md` sections, in order: 1. "What a hook is": a filter in front of one `atm task` subcommand with four results (handled, pass-through, not-applicable, refused). 2. "The request": the design §2.1 JSON, where `request` is the HTTP body of the command, and `custom`, the `--custom` object given at registration, with the design §2.1 `/jev-goal` example of one module serving many schedules. 3. "The reply": the four design §2.2 shapes, the old `success` key being malformed, actions over any command except the hook and cron registry, `as`, the D-c and D-d rules, and what the CLI prints. 4. "The module": - `TIMEOUT_MS` with its grammar and the 2 500 ms cap, and the optional `CRON_TIMEOUT_MS` for cron ticks, capped at 30 000 ms. - The design §9.8 `__main__` block. - A 40-line example implementing `task.close` and `task.assign` only. Every other `task.*` replies `{"result": "not-applicable"}`. - `cron(args)`, `stop(args)` and `doctor(request)`, with the design §9.10 doctor request and reply JSON and a `doctor` example that returns one `warning` finding. - A module returns actions rather than calling `atm` for its own hooked command. A nested `atm` call is an ordinary request bounded by the hook timeout. 5. "Errors you will see": the six codes and their exit codes. 6. "Registering": any roster member may register; any number of phases may register the same hook, and each command runs the active phases' modules oldest first until one handles; later ones are not run (design D-5). A module must answer not-applicable quickly for a task it does not own, checking its own bead and task ownership first. 7. "Cron": - The grammar of design D-g, with `0 */5 * * * *` as the example, in UTC. - No replay and one run in flight. Each schedule fires at its occurrence plus a fixed random `jitter_s` (design §5 D-r), shown by `atm cron list`. - The mandatory stop: `--until` or `--until-hook`, with the atm-bd phase-bead pattern. - `--arg`, and `atm cron end`. 8. "Doctor": one call per module, cwd, team and phase; findings appear under `hooks` with their module and phase and never change the summary. 9. "Platforms": Windows uses `python` and gets `SystemRoot` and `USERPROFILE`. A timeout kills only the child there, while unix kills the process group. ## Authoritative deliverables 1. The two commands and the rules above; the CLI validates neither the hook name nor the expression (ADR-068 D3, ADR-069 D1). 2. `read_timeout_ms` per design §9.8 (ANC-011). 3. `exit_code_for_atm_error` arms per design §9.1: the three validation codes exit 3; `HookExit`, `HookTimeout`, `HookMalformed` exit 1 through `_ => 1`. 4. `doctor_hooks::collect` per design §9.10 and the one call in `doctor()`; the section never fails doctor and never changes `summary` (ANC-015, ANC-016). `print_doctor_result` renders `Hooks:` with one line per entry (`/ : ` or the error) and one indented ` : ` line per finding, or `Hooks: none`; `--json` carries `hooks`. 5. Composition and shutdown as above (`REQ-P-CRON-002`, ADR-069 D2). 6. `cli_surface_baseline.json` regenerated for the two subtrees only. 7. The user documentation above; `cli-reference.md` lists every flag. 8. Tests, same unit, through the in-process harness of `crates/atm/tests/task_ledger_cli.rs` (no live daemon, REQ-BK-TESTS). ## Authoritative acceptance criteria `crates/atm/tests/hook_cli.rs` unless stated: - [ ] (ANC-011) `req:REQ-P-HOOK-003` `register_reads_timeout_ms_from_module` (`TIMEOUT_MS = 2500` stored); `register_refuses_bad_timeout_ms_before_any_request`: `no_timeout.py`, `zero_timeout.py`, `over_cap.py` (3000), `indented.py`, `two_lines.py` each exit 3 with `ATM_HOOK_MODULE_INVALID` and the router request counter is 0; `hook_module.rs::tests::timeout_ms_grammar` covers `TIMEOUT_MS: int = 2500 # ms` accepted and `TIMEOUT_MSX = 1` refused. - [ ] (ANC-013) `req:REQ-P-HOOK-003` `register_refuses_cron_tick_and_unknown_names_with_daemon_message`; `rg -n 'parse_task_hook|TASK_HOOKS' crates/atm/src` is empty. - [ ] (D-5) `req:REQ-P-HOOK-003` `register_second_phase_same_hook_succeeds`: with phase `bj`'s `task.close` active, `atm hook register task.close --phase bk` exits 0 and `atm hook list` shows both rows active. - [ ] (ANC-002, ANC-010) `req:REQ-P-HOOK-003` `disable_phase_keeps_rows_and_list_shows_them_inactive`; `disable_with_no_active_hooks_prints_none_and_exits_zero`; `list_json_is_a_bare_array_and_empty_is_brackets`. - [ ] (ANC-004) `req:REQ-P-HOOK-001` `task_close_refused_prints_hook_message_and_exits_nonzero` (exit 3, task still `active`) and `close_end_to_end_with_refusing_hook_leaves_task_open` through `DaemonHookRunner` and bk-3's `fixture_hook.py`; `hook_actions_response_prints_hook_ran_n_actions`. - [ ] (REQ-BK-ERRORS) `req:REQ-P-HOOK-003` `crates/atm/src/main.rs::tests::hook_and_cron_codes_map_to_documented_exit_codes`: the six codes give 3, 3, 3, 1, 1, 1 in design §9.1 order. - [ ] (ANC-015, REQ-P-HOOK-004) `req:REQ-P-HOOK-004` `doctor_hooks_section_dedupes_by_module_cwd_team_and_phase`: two hooks and one schedule on one module in phase `bk` give one entry with both names in `hooks`, the schedule in `schedules`, one runner call, `success == Some(true)` and `message == Some("ok")`; the same module registered in phase `bj` too gives a second entry and a second call; `doctor_findings_carry_module_and_phase` (a reply with one `warning` finding gives an entry with that finding, its `module_path` and `phase`, and `summary` unchanged; a malformed reply gives `error.code == ATM_HOOK_MALFORMED` and doctor exits as without hooks); `doctor_hooks_calls_run_concurrently_under_one_budget` (two `DummyHookRunner` replies released by one `Notify` only after both calls started). - [ ] (ANC-016) `req:REQ-P-HOOK-004` `doctor_hooks_section_reports_timeout_without_failing_doctor` (exit status and `summary` equal those without registrations); `doctor_hooks_section_is_empty_array_for_team_without_registrations` (`"hooks": []`). - [ ] (REQ-BK-D3) `req:REQ-P-HOOK-003` `rg -n 'process::Command' crates/atm/src/commands/hook.rs crates/atm/src/commands/cron.rs crates/atm/src/commands/hook_module.rs` is empty: the CLI only sends requests; the composition passes the one `DaemonHookRunner` from `build_replacement_handler` to `AtmCron` (`Arc::ptr_eq` asserted in `cron_scheduler_installed_once_and_cron_routes_reach_it`). - [ ] (D-2) `req:REQ-P-HOOK-004` `rg -in 'sha|\bbd\b|\.beads' crates/atm/src/commands/hook.rs crates/atm/src/commands/cron.rs crates/atm-http-runtime/src/doctor_hooks.rs` is empty. `crates/atm/tests/cron_cli.rs`: - [ ] (ANC-019, D-j) `req:REQ-P-CRON-001` `start_persists_row_with_args_and_timeout`: `--arg status --arg --json --until-hook` stores `args == ["status","--json"]`, `cron_expr` byte-identical, `timeout_ms == 2500`, `stop == Hook`; `list_shows_last_run_and_outcome_after_record_run`; `list_prints_stop_until_in_utc`. - [ ] (Rand 2026-10-18 cron timeout) `req:REQ-P-CRON-001` `cron_timeout_defaults_to_timeout_ms` (`valid_hook.py` without `CRON_TIMEOUT_MS` sends `timeout_ms == 2500`; `cron_timeout.py` sends `20000`); `cron_start_refuses_cron_timeout_above_30s` (`cron_over_cap.py` exits 3 with `ATM_HOOK_MODULE_INVALID`, request counter 0); `hook register` of `cron_timeout.py` still stores `TIMEOUT_MS` 2500. - [ ] (ANC-022, Rand 2026-10-18 custom) `req:REQ-P-CRON-001` `custom_flag_reaches_the_row`: `--custom '{"goal":"ship"}'` on `hook register` and `cron start` stores that object, `list --json` carries it and `jitter_s`, and the human table prints `1 keys` and `JITTER_S`; `custom_non_object_refused`: `--custom '[1]'` and `--custom 'x'` are clap errors naming `--custom`, request counter 0. - [ ] (ANC-023) `req:REQ-P-CRON-001` `start_refuses_missing_stop_condition_before_any_request` and `start_refuses_both_stop_conditions_before_any_request` (clap usage error, counter 0); `start_refuses_until_in_the_past_with_daemon_message`. - [ ] `req:REQ-P-CRON-001` `start_refuses_invalid_expression_with_cron_expr_invalid` (`x y` and the five-field `* * * * *`, exit 3, list empty); `start_refuses_active_duplicate_name`; `end_phase_keeps_rows_inactive_with_ended_at`. `crates/atm-daemon-bootstrap/tests/cron_composition.rs`: - [ ] (ADR-069 D2) `req:REQ-P-CRON-002` `cron_scheduler_installed_once_and_cron_routes_reach_it` (a second `install_cron_scheduler` errors); `cron_worker_starts_after_runtime_and_before_ready_signal`; `cron_worker_is_first_shutdown_step` (probe order begins `cron_worker`, `listener`); `cron_initial_load_error_aborts_startup`. - [ ] (REQ-BK-D4A) `req:REQ-P-CRON-002` `daemon_restart_with_schedule_due_while_down_fires_once_at_next_occurrence_and_not_at_startup` with `TokioClock` and a paused runtime. - [ ] (ANC-017, ANC-024) `req:REQ-P-CRON-002` `fixture_cron_receives_args_through_the_composed_scheduler`: `AtmCron` composed as above with `DaemonHookRunner` and `fixture_cron.py`; `run_now` on an `--until-hook` schedule writes the `cron.stop` request and then the `cron.tick` request with `request.args`, each with `sys.argv[1:]` equal to its hook name only, and `last_outcome == "ok"`; after the stop-marker file, `"stopped: marker present"` and `active == false`. Surface and docs: - [ ] `req:REQ-P-HOOK-003` `cargo test -p atm --test cli_surface` passes with a baseline diff of only the `hook` and `cron` subtrees; `git diff --stat` shows no change to `crates/atm/Cargo.toml`. - [ ] `req:REQ-P-USER-DOCS-001` `hooks.md` has the nine sections; its example module defines handlers for `task.close` and `task.assign` only; `cli-reference.md` has `` ### `atm cron` `` and `` ### `atm hook` ``; `just lint` (site-links) passes. ## Authoritative validation - `cargo test -p atm -p atm-http-runtime -p atm-daemon-bootstrap` - `cargo clippy -p atm -p atm-http-runtime -p atm-daemon-bootstrap --all-targets -- -D warnings` - `just lint` - `just test` ## Non-closure - No scheduler, runner, filter or route code is written here. The live-host walkthrough is the phase-ending gate's evidence.
